title: Illegal moves, irregularities and flag fall
summary: What happens after an illegal move in classical, rapid and blitz, how flag fall is decided, and when insufficient material saves you.

steps.md: An **illegal move** is completed once you press the clock. In standard games the position before the irregularity is restored, the opponent gets **two extra minutes**, and a **second** completed illegal move by the same player **loses** (unless the opponent cannot checkmate, then it is a draw). Rapid and blitz: same principle, **one minute** instead of two. Pressing the clock without moving also counts as an illegal move.

steps.question: Classical game. Your opponent leaves their king in check and presses the clock. It is their first illegal move. What happens?
choices: They lose immediately
The position before the illegal move is restored, you receive two extra minutes, and they must make a legal move (with the touched piece if possible)
You may capture their king
The game is replayed from the start
steps.explain: Art. 7.5. "Capturing the king" does not exist under FIDE rules. Touch-move still applies to the piece they touched for the illegal move, if it has a legal move.

steps.prompt: Your opponent's illegal move has just been taken back and you received two extra minutes. They then replied ...Qh4. Reset your attention to the board: what is the strongest move?
steps.explain: Nxh4 wins the queen. After any irregularity, players on both sides tend to rush; take a breath and run your normal checks, captures and threats scan before moving.

steps.question: Blitz game (supervised). Your opponent makes an illegal move and presses the clock. You notice it. What is the standard result under the current FIDE blitz rules?
choices: You can claim a win immediately for any illegal move
Same as Art. 7.5 but with one minute instead of two: first illegal move gives you one minute; a second one loses
Nothing: illegal moves stand in blitz
The game is drawn
steps.explain: App. B.3 applies Art. 7 with one minute instead of two. Many older club rules ("illegal move loses") are out of date; check the event regulations.

steps.question: Your flag falls. Your opponent has only king and bishop. What is the result?
choices: You lose on time
Draw: king and bishop cannot checkmate by any legal sequence, so the opponent cannot win on time
Draw only if you also have a bishop
The opponent wins if they claim quickly
steps.explain: Art. 6.9: flag fall loses unless the opponent cannot checkmate by any legal series of moves. With K+B vs your remaining material, check carefully: if you still have pawns or pieces, a "helpmate" may be possible (e.g. K+B vs K+P can mate in a corner with the pawn blocking), and then you lose.

steps.question: Your flag falls. Your opponent has king and knight; you have king and rook. What is the result under Art. 6.9?
choices: Draw, because a knight can never mate
You lose, because a mate is theoretically possible with your rook blocking your own king
You win on material
The arbiter decides by evaluation
steps.explain: The test is "any legal series of moves", including the worst possible play by you. With your rook available to block your own king, a knight mate exists in theory, so flag fall loses. Only bare king (or truly impossible material) saves you.

steps.question: Which counts as an illegal move under Art. 7.5?
choices: Touching a piece and not moving it
Pressing the clock without making a move
Offering a draw before pressing the clock
Adjusting a piece after saying "I adjust"
steps.explain: Art. 7.5.3: pressing the clock without moving is treated as an illegal move. Failing to follow touch-move is dealt with under Art. 4, not as an illegal move.

steps.question: Retrieval check: classical game, your opponent makes their second completed illegal move. You have only a bare king left. Result?
choices: They lose
Draw, because you cannot checkmate
Two more minutes for you
The game continues normally
steps.explain: The second illegal move normally loses, but if the opponent of the offender cannot checkmate by any legal sequence, the game is drawn (Art. 7.5.5).

sources: FIDE Laws of Chess (2023) Art. 6.9, 7.2-7.5, App. A.3, B.3
